column2: The plundering and looting by your fleets has earned you a name as a fearsome pirate. All along the coasts, mothers tucking their children in for the night warn them that unless they behave, the terrible Captain [Root.GetFirstName], scourge of the seas, will come ashore with [Root.GetHerHis] dire sea dogs and take them away. In the taverns of Sartosa they drink to [Root.GetHerHim].
Arrr, mateys!

You were in [Root.Location.GetName], a harbour known to be prowled by pirates, and had taken ship along the coast when a small fleet was spotted bearing down on you. The crew realised too late that it was a pirate flotilla. Your ship is taken, along with all its crew, and you are the greatest prize of all.
I hope this [From.GetTitle] will take a ransom.

A small flotilla under one of your lesser captains was prowling the seas near [From.Location.GetName] when it came upon a lightly defended ship. The captain reports that the ship and crew were taken without much trouble, and that one passenger was of noble blood. [From.GetSheHeCap] names [From.GetHerHim]self [From.GetTitledFirstName] [From.GetOnlyDynastyName].
Good work. A most valuable prisoner.

Grave news: your [GetFromRelation] [From.GetTitledFirstName] [From.GetOnlyDynastyName] was at sea near [From.Location.GetName] when pirates fell upon the ship! [From.GetSheHeCap] and the crew are now said to be the captives of [FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName]. A go-between from the pirate's ship has already named a price.
Pay the ransom and bring [From.GetHerHim] home.
This [FromFrom.Culture.GetName] menace will hang for it!
A New Pirate Lord

After the death of the dreaded [former_captain.GetBestName], the First Mate [designated_heir.GetTitledFirstName] has already taken up every duty of the Lord Captain of [designated_heir.GetPrimaryTitle.GetName]. By right the ships should all be yours, but the crews have sworn to the new Pirate Lord, and the code of the sea counts for more aboard than any law of inheritance.
Let the First Mate have the ships. I keep the name.
Then I will sail as the First Mate!
Fit Out a Plunder Fleet

Give [Root.GetFirstName], one of the cutthroats at your court, ships, a crew and a Letter of Plunder, and send [Root.GetHerHim] out to raid in your name. Each year half of what the fleet takes comes home to you. The sea is wide and the hoard grows, and a captain far from home may come to wonder why [Root.GetSheHe] shares it at all...

[Root.GetFirstName] sails as captain of a plunder fleet: a raiding host, a fleet of galleys and two mates. Each year half of the fleet's plunder comes to you. After five years at sea the captain may come home with the hoard, or keep the ships and turn free raider.
You do not already have a plunder fleet at sea
Plunder Fleet
Enables a targeted decision on a courtier of your own: fit out a plunder fleet that raids in your name and sends you half the booty every year.
[Root.GetFirstName]'s Plunder Fleet
Plunder Fleet
Plunder Fleets
Patron of the Fleet

My [From.GetTitledFirstName] sends greetings from the sea, and your share. The purser has counted it twice, and the crew grumbled only a little. The coasts burn, the merchantmen strike their colours at the sight of our sails, and every tavern from Sartosa to Copher drinks to your name.

Sent from the deck of your fleet,
[From.GetFirstName]
A fine haul. Keep them sailing.

Word comes from the harbour: [From.GetTitledFirstName] has struck your colours and hoisted [From.GetHerHis] own. The fleet you paid for, the crews you hired and the plunder that was yours by right now sail for [From.GetHerHim] alone. In the taverns of Sartosa they laugh about it, and say a Legend who trusts a pirate deserves no better.
Put a price on [From.GetHerHis] head. Every crew in the Brethren will hunt [From.GetHerHim].
The sea takes back its own. Let [From.GetHerHim] go.

I write with ill news. Your plunder fleet is no more. The galleys are at the bottom of the sea or scattered to every port that will take them, and the captain, [From.GetTitledFirstName], is a prisoner or a beggar on some foreign quay. What is left of the crew has drunk the last of the plunder.\n\nYour harbourmaster
Curse the sea and all who sail it.

After long years of raiding, [From.GetTitledFirstName] brings your plunder fleet home. The galleys sit low in the water. Chests of coin, bolts of silk, Arabyan spices, holy plate from Tilean shrines and a hold full of prisoners for the slave pens come ashore while the whole harbour watches. The captain kneels on the quay and lays the hoard at your feet, as was agreed.\n\nIt is not every day a pirate keeps a bargain.
Welcome home, captain. Drink, all of you!
